yaml:
agents:
  - name: Developer
    model: default
  - name: Checker
    model: default
flow:
  - id: validate
    name: Validate
    kind: check
    by: agent
    agent: Checker
    skill: validate
    rounds: 3
    fail_to: Dev
    description: "Checks the work against the ticket and runs the project's checks, so what Dev missed is caught before anyone reviews it."
  - id: dev
    name: Dev
    kind: agent
    agent: Developer
    skill: work-ticket
    description: "Builds what the ticket asks for, with its tests, and commits it: every ticket that changes the code needs it."
  - id: review
    name: Review
    kind: check
    by: you
    description: "The user reads the change and passes it, or sends it back with what to fix: their say before it is delivered."
delivery:
  delivers: either
  mode: click
  agent: Developer
  skill: open-pr

agent.label: Agent

picker.title: Pick a skill…

items.label: address-review
items.hint: Otaq’s · Address the review feedback on the Otaq ticket named by $OTAQ_TICKET after the user sent it back - get the context and the user's comment with `otaq prime`, read the line comments with `otaq review feedback`, fix them, commit everything, then end your stage again with a short comment through `otaq stage next`.

items.label: answer-question
items.hint: Otaq’s · Answer a linked Otaq ticket's question from this finished ticket's conversation - get the context with `otaq prime`, answer only (change nothing), and reply with `otaq answer <ID> --stdin`.

items.label: commit
items.hint: Otaq’s · Otaq's default Commit workflow skill - commit every change in this worktree (messages as the project's rules and the Agent instructions say, else "<KEY>: <what changed>"), before `otaq stage next`.

items.label: flow
items.hint: Otaq’s · Change an Otaq project's board flow as Noyan - read the current flow with `otaq flow show`, write the whole flow file (agents and stages, every field), give each stage a description of what it settles and when it matters, put the reason for each stage you add or change (with its source) in the proposal's `why:`, propose it with `otaq flow propose --stdin`, then end your turn and wait for the user's Apply, Cancel or Ask for more changes as your next message.

items.label: milestone-plan
items.hint: Otaq’s · An agent writes the ticket’s plan: the pieces, their order and what each waits for.

items.label: noyan
items.hint: Otaq’s · Work as Noyan, an Otaq project's coordinator - read `otaq prime --project`, name this conversation after the first request, take a light look at the code without editing or committing, write tickets whose notes hand on where the code lives, what you saw and the open questions, file several tickets only for separate deliverables, pass on only the stage choices the user names, and file them in Backlog with the otaq CLI.

items.label: open-pr
items.hint: Otaq’s · A pull request opens on GitHub; your team reviews it there.

items.label: product-spec
items.hint: Otaq’s · An agent asks you what to build, for whom and why, then writes down what you agreed.

items.label: push
items.hint: Otaq’s · Otaq's default Push workflow skill - get the context with `otaq prime`, propose messages for the commits not yet on the PR's branch with `otaq pr propose --stdin`, and only once Otaq says they are confirmed (by the user, or at once in automatic mode) push them to the existing PR, then report it with `otaq pr opened <url>`.

items.label: restack
items.hint: Otaq’s · Bring the Otaq ticket named by $OTAQ_TICKET up to date with the branch it merges into - get the context with `otaq prime`, rebase onto the target it names, resolve the conflicts, commit, then end your stage with a short comment through `otaq stage next`.

items.label: tech-spec
items.hint: Otaq’s · An agent works out how to build it, asking you where a choice matters, and writes it down.

items.label: validate
items.hint: Otaq’s · A checking agent runs the tests and lint. If something fails, the ticket goes back to the stage before.

items.label: work-ticket
items.hint: Otaq’s · An agent writes the code in the ticket’s own copy of the repo (a worktree).

ask.label: Ask the agent to write it…
ask.hint: Starts Noyan on the right and uses tokens.
